invariants.pyCode:
def M7_S1_NoDualLeaderPerTerm():
    for term in range(1, MAX_TERM + 1):
        leaders_at_term = 0
        for node_id in range(NUM_CONTROL_NODES):
            n = nodes[node_id]
            if n.node_role == "leader" and n.current_term == term:
                leaders_at_term = leaders_at_term + 1
        if leaders_at_term > 1:
            return False
    return True

# M7-S2: Leader-only write gating — a lease grant / workload-catalog write /
# shard-assignment write is only ever accepted by the ObjectStore attributed
# to the node that was actually elected leader for that term. Checked as a
# genuine cross-action comparison: `accepted_write_by_term[T]` is written by
# FinishWrite, `leader_at_term[T]` is written by BecomeLeader — two
# independent actions, so a bug that attributed an accepted write to the
# wrong node/term (e.g. a captured_term/node_id mixup, or skipping
# `term_matches_current`/`term_valid_for_store`) is falsifiable by exhaustive
# BFS — unlike a first draft of this net, which set `accepted_term =
# captured_term` and then compared `captured_term != accepted_term`
# immediately after that same assignment: always vacuously false, caught
# only by deliberately breaking FinishWrite's guard and observing the old
# check stayed green regardless.
#
# Scope note: this cross-check cannot independently re-verify the
# `is_leader_now` conjunct specifically (whether the writing node's role was
# still exactly "leader" at the instant FinishWrite ran) without re-reading
# the same `node_role` FinishWrite itself reads — there is no other state
# that records "was this node's role Leader at this exact instant" (a
# snapshot fact, not a monotonic ledger entry), so, unlike the term/identity
# conjuncts, that one relies on FinishWrite's own correctly-written,
# freshly-read `n.node_role == "leader"` check (verified by inspection: it
# reads live per-node state mutated only by StartElection / RequestVoteAnd-
# Grant / BecomeLeader / CrashLeader, never by FinishWrite itself). What
# exhaustive BFS *does* additionally verify here is that no interleaving of
# concurrent crash/election/write actions around that correctly-written
# guard can still produce a same-term dual acceptance or a wrong-identity
# acceptance (M7-S1's dual-leader freedom is exactly the complementary
# guarantee this leans on).

invariants.name: M7_S2_LeaderOnlyWriteAccepted
invariants.pyCode:
def M7_S2_LeaderOnlyWriteAccepted():
    for term in range(1, MAX_TERM + 1):
        accepted_by = accepted_write_by_term[term]
        if accepted_by != -1 and accepted_by != leader_at_term[term]:
            return False
    return True

# M7-S3: Composed shard-fence fencing — a shard's fence-epoch write (the
# `is_shard_fence_write` write, whose token is derived from
# (raft_term, control_leader_id) per the header comment) is only accepted
# from the node that was actually elected leader for that term. Same
# cross-action structure as M7-S2, over the shard-fence-specific ledger.
# Because both write families share one CAS pair (accepted_term /
# accepted_leader), at most one write — of either family — can ever be the
# currently accepted one: no split-brain shard grant can occur.

invariants.name: M7_S3_ShardFenceComposedWithLeaderEpoch
invariants.pyCode:
def M7_S3_ShardFenceComposedWithLeaderEpoch():
    for term in range(1, MAX_TERM + 1):
        accepted_by = shard_fence_accepted_write_by_term[term]
        if accepted_by != -1 and accepted_by != leader_at_term[term]:
            return False
    return True

def count_votes(nodes, candidate_id):
    c = nodes[candidate_id]
    count = 0
    for node_id in range(len(nodes)):
        if nodes[node_id].voted_for == candidate_id and nodes[node_id].current_term == c.current_term:
            count = count + 1
    return count

# True if some *other* node is currently a candidate. Used to serialize
# elections (see the state-space/liveness design note below) — this is the
# abstraction this model uses in place of Raft's real randomized-timeout
# desynchronization mechanism, which is out of scope to model faithfully at
# this abstraction level (FIZZBEE_TEST_PLAN.md §2.4 "SimNetwork fidelity
# boundary": timing/randomization gaps are documented, not silently assumed
# away).

def any_other_candidate(nodes, self_id):
    for i in range(len(nodes)):
        if i != self_id and nodes[i].node_role == "candidate":
            return True
    return False

# True if some node currently believes itself Leader. A real Raft follower
# resets its election timeout on every heartbeat/AppendEntries from a live
# leader, so it never starts a spurious election while a functioning leader
# exists; this model does not represent heartbeats explicitly, so
# StartElection uses this check as the direct stand-in. Without it, an
# exhaustive-BFS worst case has a follower call StartElection immediately
# after a perfectly healthy first leader is elected, burning the entire
# MAX_ELECTIONS budget on a spurious re-election and leaving none for the
# post-crash recovery this spec exists to prove.
